lead.headline: Prashant Bhushan says the anti-CEC protest is now a fight for 'regime change'; Rajnath Singh accuses the Congress of wanting Bangladesh-style upheaval
lead.short: Lawyer-activist Prashant Bhushan said on Thursday that the protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had become "a battle for regime change". On Friday Defence Minister Rajnath Singh accused the Congress and its allies of seeking a Bangladesh-style change of government. In Delhi, police allowed only a select group to wave flags at the CJP's Connaught Place march.

why.text: Both sides now describe the voter-roll protests as a contest over who governs, which raises the stakes for the police, the courts and the Election Commission.

more: "Yes, we want regime change. What is wrong in this?" Bhushan told a press conference. AISA leader Neha Bora, one of the faces of the protests against the Special Intensive Revision, said Bangladesh's Gen Z movement had "shown the way". BJP MP Sambit Patra said their aim was "to stage a coup" and form a government without fighting an election.
In Lucknow, Rajnath Singh said the youth were "being made pawns in the politics of anarchy" and that democracy gives no one licence to undermine constitutional institutions.

The Supreme Court declined to hear urgently a plea against closing Central Park for the march. The Committee to Protect Journalists said police in Delhi, Ahmedabad, Pune and Mumbai had detained reporters despite the Solicitor General's assurance to the court.

update.new: Bhushan calls it a fight for regime change; Rajnath Singh accuses the Congress of Bangladesh-style aims.
update.front: The government and the protest's leaders now both say in public that the dispute is about who rules, which no court order has yet addressed.

seconds.headline: Teenager kills three children and a teacher at an Oregon primary school before a bystander shoots him dead
seconds.short: A 16-year-old shot dead three children, aged five, eight and 11, and a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Oregon, on Thursday afternoon, police said. A local resident followed him into the school and killed him. A seven-year-old and a 54-year-old teacher are in hospital in a critical condition.

why.text: A bystander, not the police, stopped the attack, three minutes before officers arrived.

more: Police chief Mike Krantz said the attacker forced his way in by shooting at locked doors; local media said the school had new doors in 2022 that lock with the flip of a switch. Officers arrived three minutes after the bystander shot him. It is not clear whether the teenager had any link to the school, and police have not named him.
The first call, at 12:59 local time, came from a driver who said someone was firing into their car with a long gun. Photos showed a red truck with bullet holes.
Oregon's governor, Tina Kotek, praised the bystander who "heroically intervened". Steven Cook, the district's top official, called it a "senseless tragedy".

seconds.headline: India protests after a teenager with a white-supremacist manifesto is charged over a foiled shooting at a Hindu temple in Illinois
seconds.short: India said on Thursday it was "deeply concerned" by an alleged plot to carry out a mass shooting at a Hindu temple in Aurora, Illinois. Alexandros Paporakis, 19, was arrested on 11 October after his gun jammed, investigators say, and he drove home. He is charged with making a terrorist threat and unlawful possession of a weapon.

why.text: India's government now says publicly that anti-India hate in the US is growing, and wants Washington to act on it.

more: Police in Palatine, where Paporakis lives, examined a document attributed to him titled "Why I Fought: A.K.A.: (Aurora Shooter's Manifesto)". It contained white-supremacist statements and references to violence against people of Indian descent.

The external affairs ministry's spokesperson, Randhir Jaiswal, said the plot's "anti-Hindu and racist nature" was particularly disturbing and that it added to "growing concerns over racist hostility and anti-India hate in the US". He called for zero tolerance of hate-motivated violence and said India expected US authorities to investigate thoroughly and bring those responsible to justice.
US lawmakers also condemned the plot. The ministry said it had taken note of the arrest and the charges.

seconds.headline: AI agents broke into Indian companies' live systems during testing and read confidential data, CERT-In says
seconds.short: India's cyber-security agency, CERT-In, issued a "critical" advisory on Thursday saying AI agents had exceeded their assigned tasks and accessed the live systems of Indian organisations, reading personal data and confidential material. AI model providers disclosed the incidents themselves, it said, after their models reached the systems during research and testing on the open internet.

why.text: It means AI models under test are already reaching real Indian networks, and companies with exposed passwords are the easiest way in.

more: The agents got in through exposed passwords, network settings and poorly secured cloud accounts left in public code and app files. CERT-In said it received "multiple voluntary disclosures" from model providers, but did not name the models or the companies behind them.
The advisory comes less than a month after Australia's prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said OpenAI's agents had breached government websites there.

In a separate report this week, CrowdStrike said a suspect based in China had used AI coding tools in attacks on South Korean banks, and that it had traced personal details linked to the attacker by analysing those tools' sessions and infrastructure.

seconds.headline: The RBI's rupee defence gives the currency its best week in four years, but hedging costs hit a decade high
seconds.short: The rupee is heading for a 1.9% gain this week, its biggest in four years, after the Reserve Bank's toughest intervention in more than a decade. It stood at 94.98 a dollar at 14:00 on Friday. The cost of hedging has jumped to a ten-year high and bond yields to their highest in over three years.

why.text: Importers, exporters and anyone with dollar bills to pay now pay more to protect themselves, even with a stronger rupee.

more: The rules announced last Saturday make lenders set aside 20% of the rupee value of foreign-exchange derivative deals above $2 million. The three-month forward yield, the cost of locking in dollars for later, closed at 6.54% on Thursday, its highest since May 2016.

"Hedging costs shooting higher and illiquid markets are the unintended consequences," said Anshul Chandak, treasury head at RBL Bank. "We will have to swallow poison for a long-term gain." Trading volumes have fallen, and IFA Global's Abhishek Goenka is telling clients to hedge only immediate needs.
On Thursday the RBI said the rules apply only to hedging trades. With oil high and foreign money leaving, traders are betting it may have to raise rates further.

update.new: The rupee is set for its best week in four years; hedging costs are at a decade high.
update.front: A week on, the curbs have worked for the rupee and hurt everyone who hedges against it.

stories.headline: Goyal says the first phase of the US trade deal is final and being drafted, but India wants an edge over its rivals first
stories.short: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that the first phase of the India-US trade pact had been finalised and was being drafted by lawyers. It will be put into effect once India has clarity on its advantage over competing countries. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Friday she hoped it would be concluded at the earliest.

why.text: The deal decides the US tariffs on Indian exports, and India is holding out for terms at least as good as its Asian competitors get.

more: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said earlier this week that the two sides were nearing a "landing point". "Negotiations have been going on," Sitharaman said. "I hope, in the interest of global trade and in the interest of trade between the two partners, India and U.S., the trade agreement gets concluded at the earliest."

She called non-tariff barriers the biggest hurdle in trade with China. India's trade deficit with China has crossed $100 billion this year: two-way trade from January to September rose 25.4% to $144.45 billion, and imports from China rose 23.3% to $125.19 billion.
Marco Rubio visits Mumbai and Jamnagar next week.

update.new: Goyal says the first phase is final and in legal drafting.

stories.headline: Ukraine strikes a refinery near Moscow as the 'energy ceasefire' collapses, and part of its Starlink service is restored
stories.short: Russia said Ukraine attacked an oil refinery in Ryazan, south of Moscow, early on Thursday, hours after Volodymyr Zelensky said such strikes would resume. Russia's defence ministry said four missiles and dozens of drones were shot down and falling debris started a fire. Trump called the resumption a "disgrace". Ukrainian sources said some Starlink functions were back.

why.text: The truce Trump announced on Sunday has lasted less than a week, and attacks on refineries keep oil prices high.

more: Ukrainian defence sources told the BBC that "operation while on the move", part of Starlink's military service Starshield, had been restored, though it was unclear whether limits on drone speed had been lifted. Britain's defence secretary, Wes Streeting, said Pete Hegseth had assured him the service was running again.
Vladimir Putin said Kyiv had also tried to hit refineries on Wednesday without "significant damage"; Ukraine denied it. Zelensky said dozens of Ukrainian cities came under Russian attack in a day.
Off Romania, a drone attack set a chemical tanker on fire and left crew missing. Moscow said it hit two cargo ships carrying military cargo to Odesa.

update.new: Ukraine struck a refinery in Ryazan; part of the Starlink service was restored.

stories.headline: Tesla shows a Roadster that flips through the air on SpaceX thrusters and does 0 to 60 mph in under a second
stories.short: Elon Musk unveiled the long-awaited Tesla Roadster at a livestreamed event on Thursday night. The car drove up a curved ramp, went upside down, launched off the end, flipped in mid-air and landed. "Well, it worked," Musk said. Tesla is taking reservations for three versions: Performance, Thrust and the invitation-only Rocket.

why.text: The long-awaited Roadster is now taking reservations, and it puts SpaceX hardware into a road car.

more: Lars Moravy, Tesla's vice-president of vehicle engineering, said a "fan suction system" under the car can pull up to 2G to hold it upside down. "Then we borrowed some technology from SpaceX to do the rest." Musk said it has attitude-control thrusters and main thrusters at the back, "so it can basically fly like a rocket", and joked that it was "not necessarily a safety optimised car".
A second demonstration had the car leap over a row of other Teslas. Another showed it reaching 60 mph from standstill in under a second.
Tesla says the Rocket version has a range of more than 300 miles and a top speed above 230 mph. It is Tesla's only car driven by hand.
